proposals.before: Also because in the second year of Yuanfu an immortal crane at the temple of Lord Wuyi welcomed an edict, and in the second year of Zhenghe, when ministers were feasted at Yanfu Palace, a flock of cranes came from the northwest and circled above Rui Mo Hall, and flying cranes repeatedly appeared when the Dasheng music was performed, an edict ordered the creation of the Auspicious Crane flag.
proposals.after: Also because in the second year of Yuanfu an immortal crane at the temple of Lord Wuyi welcomed an edict, and in the second year of Zhenghe, when ministers were feasted at Yanfu Palace, a flock of cranes came from the northwest and circled above Ruimo Hall, and flying cranes repeatedly appeared when the Dasheng music was performed, an edict ordered the creation of the Auspicious Crane flag.
proposals.reason: 睿謨殿 is the hall name Ruimo; splitting it as 'Rui Mo Hall' obscures the proper noun.

proposals.before: In the eighth year, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Bangchang memorialized: "In the time of Emperor Taizu, sweet dew fell at Jiangling for ten days, auspicious wheat with six ears appeared at Puyang, a golden parrot was captured on the Long Plateau, three jade rabbits were obtained at Yun Prefecture, tame elephants arrived when the Five Ridges were pacified, and a white deer appeared when the Qiong tribes submitted. All of these were ordered made into flags and displayed.
proposals.after: In the eighth year of Zhenghe, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Bangchang memorialized: "In the time of Emperor Taizu, sweet dew fell at Jiangling for ten days, auspicious wheat with six ears appeared at Puyang, a golden parrot was captured on the Long Plateau, three jade rabbits were obtained at Yun Prefecture, tame elephants arrived when the Five Ridges were pacified, and a white deer appeared when the Qiong administration submitted. All of these were ordered made into flags and displayed.
proposals.reason: Bare 'eighth year' inherits the preceding Zhenghe narrative and should be dated; 瓊管 is the Qiong administration, not a tribal ethnonym.

proposals.before: In the seventh year of Yuanyou, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: The Kaiyuan Rites prescribe an octagonal purple umbrella for the grand procession and four-cornered green umbrellas for princes, dukes, and those below.
proposals.after: In the seventh year of Yuanyou under Emperor Zhezong, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: The Kaiyuan Rites prescribe an octagonal purple umbrella for the grand procession and four-cornered green umbrellas for princes, dukes, and those below.
proposals.reason: Chinese 哲宗元祐七年 names Emperor Zhezong; the idiomatic English omits that reigning emperor.

proposals.before: Sheep-carriage attendants wore hanging-ear topknots, green headcloths, green embroidered large-sleeve shirts, trousers, waist sashes, and green ear-shoes.

proposals.reason: Chinese 駕羊車童子 identifies youthful boys (童子), not generic attendants; the idiomatic English loses that age/role distinction.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Jianlong, Fan Zhi proposed: According to the Kaiyuan Rites, when military officers stood attendance at the great guard formation, they added teng-snake doublets like sleeves without a body to cover the upper arms, sewn under the armpit.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Jianlong under Emperor Taizu, Fan Zhi proposed: According to the Kaiyuan Rites, when military officers stood attendance at the great guard formation, they added teng-snake doublets like sleeves without a body to cover the upper arms, sewn under the armpit.
proposals.reason: Chinese opens with 太祖建隆四年, naming Emperor Taizu as the reign context; the idiomatic English omits 太祖 entirely.
